name: Sikaflex PRO+

SIKAFLEX® PRO+: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sikaflex® PRO+, April 2023, Version 01.02 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/y/sikaflex_pro_.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sikaflex® PRO+ where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02).
1.2 Product description. Sikaflex® PRO+ is a 1-component, moisture-curing, elastic joint sealant.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. Sikaflex® PRO+ is designed for movement and connection joints in concrete and masonry facades.
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.6.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sikaflex® PRO+
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: SEALANT FOR CONCRETE AND MASONRY FACADES
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Sustainability.
    - EMICODE EC1PLUS R
    - LEED® EQc 4.1
    - SCAQMD, Rule 1168
    - BAAQMD, Reg. 8, Rule 51
2.3 Approvals / certificates.
    - ASTM C 920 class 35
    - ISO 11600 F 25 HM
    - EN 15651-1 F EXT-INT CC 25 HM
2.4 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - ASTM C 719: cited elsewhere in the data sheet; test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Characteristics / Advantages (p.1); Product Information > Movement capability (p.2).
    - ASTM C 920: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - ISO 11600: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - EN 15651-1: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - ISO 1183-1: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Density (p.1).
    - ISO 868: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Shore A hardness (p.1).
    - ISO 8339: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Secant tensile modulus (p.1).
    - ISO 9047: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Movement capability (p.2).
    - ISO 7389: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Elastic recovery (p.2).
    - ISO 7390: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Sag flow (p.2).
    - CQP 049-2: Sika internal procedure reference, not a published standard. Where: Product Information > Curing rate (p.2).
    - CQP 019-1: Sika internal procedure reference, not a published standard. Where: Product Information > Skinning time (p.2).
    - CQP 019-2: Sika internal procedure reference, not a published standard. Where: Product Information > Tooling time (p.2).
2.5 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Movement capability of ± 35% (ASTM C 719)
    - Bubble-free curing
    - Good workability
    - Good adhesion to many substrates
    - Solvent-free
    - Very low emissions
2.6 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: i-Cure® Technology polyurethane
    - Colour: White, Concrete Grey, Black, Dark Grey, Sandstone, Japan Beige, Brick Red, Off White; Not all colours are available in all packaging sizes.
    - Density: 1.40 kg/l approx. (ISO 1183-1)
2.7 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Shore A hardness: 28 approx. (after 28 days) (ISO 868)
    - Secant tensile modulus: 0.50 N/mm2 approx. at 100% elongation (23 °C ); 1.15 N/mm2 approx. at 100% elongation (−20 °C) (ISO 8339)
    - Tensile strain at break: 800% approx. (ISO 37)
    - Movement capability: ± 25%; ± 35% (ISO 9047) (ASTM C 719)
    - Elastic recovery: 90% approx. (ISO 7389)
    - Tear propagation resistance: 6.5 N/mm approx. (ISO 34)
    - Service temperature: −40 °C to +70 °C
    - Resistance to weathering: 8 (ISO / DIS 19862)
    - Backing material: Use closed cell, polyethylene foam backing rods.
    - Skinning time: 70 minutes approx. (23 °C / 50% r.h.) (CQP 019-1)
    - Tooling time: 60 minutes approx. (23 °C / 50% r.h.) (CQP 019-2)
2.8 Joint design. The joint width must be designed to suit the joint movement required and the movement capability of the sealant. The joint width shall be ≥ 10 mm and ≤ 50 mm. A width to depth ratio of 2:1 must be maintained (for exceptions, see table below). Standard joint widths for joints between concrete elements
    | Joint Distance [m] | Min. Joint Width [mm] | Min. Joint Depth [mm] |
    | 2 | 10 | 10 |
    | 4 | 15 | 10 |
    | 6 | 20 | 10 |
    | 8 | 30 | 15 |
    | 10 | 35 | 17 |
    All joints must be properly designed and dimensioned in accordance with the relevant standards, before construction. Basis for calculation of the necessary joint width are the technical values of the joint sealant and the adjacent building materials, as well as the exposure of the building, type of construction and its dimensions. For larger joints please contact our Technical Service Department.
2.9 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 300 ml cartridge, 12 cartridges per box; 600 ml foil pack, 20 foil packs per box
    - Shelf life: Sikaflex® PRO+ has a shelf life of 15 months from the date of production, if it is stored in undamaged, original, sealed packaging, and if the storage conditions are met.
    - Storage conditions: Sikaflex® PRO+ shall be stored in dry conditions, where it is protected from direct sunlight and at temperatures between +5 °C and +25 °C.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate preparation.
    - The substrate must be clean, dry, sound and homogeneous, free from oils, grease, dust and loose or friable particles. Sikaflex® PRO+ adheres without primers and/or activators.
    - However, for optimum adhesion and critical, high performance applications, such as on multi-story buildings, highly stressed joints, extreme weather exposure or water immersion, the following priming and/or pretreatment procedures must be followed:
    - Non-porous substrates
    - Aluminium, anodised aluminium, stainless steel, galvanised steel, powder coated metals or glazed tiles have to be cleaned and pre-treated using Sika® Aktivator-205, wiped on with a clean towel. Before sealing, allow a flash-off time of > 15 minutes (< 6 hours). Other metals, such as copper, brass and titanium-zinc, also have to be cleaned and pre-treated using Sika® Aktivator-205,wiped on with a clean towel. After the necessary flash-off time, use a brush to apply Sika® Primer-3 N and allow a further flash-off time of > 30 minutes (< 8 hours) before sealing the joints. PVC has to be cleaned and pre-treated using Sika® Primer-215 applied with a brush. Before sealing, allow a flash-off time of > 30 minutes (< 8 hours).
    - Porous substrates
    - Concrete, aerated concrete and cement based renders, mortars and bricks shall be primed using Sika® Primer-3 N applied with a brush. Before sealing, allow a flash-off time of > 30 minutes (< 8 hours).
    - For more detailed advice and instructions please contact the local Sika Technical Services Department. Note: Primers are adhesion promoters. They are neither a substitute for the correct cleaning of a surface, nor do they improve the strength of the surface significantly.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Sag flow: 0 mm (20 mm profile, 50 °C) (ISO 7390)
    - Curing rate: 3 mm/24 hours approx. (23 °C / 50% r.h.) (CQP 049-2)
4.3 Consumption.
    | Joint length [m] | Joint width [mm] | Joint depth [mm] |
    | per 600 ml foil pack |
    | 6 | 10 | 10 |
    | 4 | 15 | 10 |
    | 3 | 20 | 10 |
    | 2 | 25 | 12 |
    | 1.3 | 30 | 15 |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
4.4 Application method / tools.
    - Sikaflex® PRO+ is supplied ready to use. After the necessary substrate preparation, insert a suitable backing rod to the required depth and apply any primer if necessary. Insert a foil pack or cartridge into the sealant gun and extrude Sikaflex® PRO+ into the joint making sure that it comes into full contact with the sides of the joint and avoids any air entrapment. Sikaflex® PRO+ sealant must be firmly tooled against the joint sides to ensure adequate adhesion. It is recommended to use masking tape where exact joint lines or neat lines are required. Remove the tape within the skin time. Do not use tooling products containing solvents. If Sikaflex® PRO+ is dry-tooled it shows a slightly structured, concrete-like surface. If it is wet-tooled (using a compatible tooling agent, e.g. Sika® Tooling Agent N) it shows a smooth surface.
    - Use a compatible tooling agent (e.g. Sika® Tooling Agent N) to smooth the joint surfaces. Do not use tooling products containing solvents.
4.5 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all tools and application equipment immediately after use with Sika® Remover-208. Once cured, residual material can only be removed mechanically.
4.6 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Sikaflex® PRO+ can be overpainted with most conventional facade coating paint systems. However, paints must first be tested to ensure compatibility by carrying out preliminary trials (e.g. according to ISO technical paper: Paintability and Paint Compatibility of Sealants). The best over-painting results are obtained when the sealant is allowed to fully cure first. Note: non-flexible paint systems may impair the elasticity of the sealant and lead to cracking of the paint film.
    - Colour variations may occur due to exposure to chemicals, high temperatures and/or UV-radiation (especially with the colour shade white). However, a change in colour is purely of aesthetic nature and does not adversely influence the technical performance or durability of the product.
    - Do not use Sikaflex® PRO+ on natural stone. Do not use Sikaflex® PRO+ on bituminous substrates, natural rubber, EPDM rubber or on any building materials which might bleed oils, plasticizers or solvents that could attack the sealant.
    - Do not use Sikaflex® PRO+ to seal joints in and around swimming pools.
    - Do not use Sikaflex® PRO+ for joints under water pressure or for permanent water immersion.
    - Do not expose uncured Sikaflex® PRO+ to alcohol containing products as this may interfere with the curing reaction.
4.7 Further information.
    - Material Data Sheet (SDS)
    - Pre-treatment Chart Sealing & Bonding
    - Method Statement Joint Sealing
    - Method Statement Joint Maintenance, Cleaning and Renovation
    - Technical Manual Facade Sealing

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. +5 °C to +40 °C, min. 3 °C above dew point temperature
5.3 Substrate temperature. +5 °C to +40 °C
5.4 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.6):
    - Colour variations may occur due to exposure to chemicals, high temperatures and/or UV-radiation (especially with the colour shade white). However, a change in colour is purely of aesthetic nature and does not adversely influence the technical performance or durability of the product.
5.5 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Density: 1.40 kg/l approx. (ISO 1183-1)
    - Shore A hardness: 28 approx. (after 28 days) (ISO 868)
    - Secant tensile modulus: 0.50 N/mm2 approx. at 100% elongation (23 °C ); 1.15 N/mm2 approx. at 100% elongation (−20 °C) (ISO 8339)
    - Tensile strain at break: 800% approx. (ISO 37)
    - Movement capability: ± 25%; ± 35% (ISO 9047) (ASTM C 719)
    - Elastic recovery: 90% approx. (ISO 7389)
    - Tear propagation resistance: 6.5 N/mm approx. (ISO 34)
    - Resistance to weathering: 8 (ISO / DIS 19862)
    - Sag flow: 0 mm (20 mm profile, 50 °C) (ISO 7390)
    - Curing rate: 3 mm/24 hours approx. (23 °C / 50% r.h.) (CQP 049-2)
    - Skinning time: 70 minutes approx. (23 °C / 50% r.h.) (CQP 019-1)
    - Tooling time: 60 minutes approx. (23 °C / 50% r.h.) (CQP 019-2)
5.6 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.7 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sikaflex® PRO+, April 2023, Version 01.02, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/y/sikaflex_pro_.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: Sikaflex Pro+, version 09/04/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/q/MSDS%20Sikaflex%20Pro%2B%20GHS7.pdf
    - Certificate: Test Certificate Sikaflex Pro Plus, version 30/09/2021, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/1/TestCert%20%20Sikaflex%20Pro%20plus.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
